# Copilot / AI Agent Instructions

This project is a Vite + React + TypeScript storefront scaffold using shadcn-ui and Tailwind. The file structure and runtime conventions below are distilled from the codebase so an AI agent can be immediately productive.

1) Big picture
- Frontend-only web app (no backend in this repo). Routes and pages live in `src/pages` and are mounted in `src/App.tsx` with `react-router-dom`.
- Global state: lightweight client state (cart) implemented in `src/context/CartContext.tsx` and persisted to `localStorage` under key `"cart"`.
- Server-state/caching: `@tanstack/react-query` is used; the `QueryClient` is created in `src/App.tsx`.
- UI primitives: the `src/components/ui/` directory contains shared atomic components (shadcn-style). Higher-level components are in `src/components`.

2) Important files & patterns (quick references)
- Entry: `src/main.tsx` (wraps `App` with `ThemeProvider`).
- Routing: `src/App.tsx` — add new app routes here and place them above the catch-all `"*"` route. Example: `<Route path="/product/:id" element={<ProductDetail />} />`.
- Cart logic: `src/context/CartContext.tsx` — exposes `useCart()` and persists to `localStorage`.
- Product data: `src/data/products.ts` (seed/demo data used by pages/components).
- Aliases: imports use `@` to reference `src` (see `vite.config.ts` `resolve.alias`). Use `import X from "@/path"`.
- UI components: `src/components/ui/*` follow shadcn naming and re-export patterns (look at `toaster.tsx`, `button.tsx`, `input.tsx` for examples).

3) Build / development / lint commands
- Install: `npm i` (Node + npm required). The README mentions using `nvm` if needed.
- Dev server: `npm run dev` — Vite dev server listens on port `8080` and host `::` (see `vite.config.ts`). Access at `http://localhost:8080`.
- Build: `npm run build` (production build). `npm run build:dev` builds with `--mode development` for debugging built output.
- Preview: `npm run preview` to preview a production build locally.
- Lint: `npm run lint` (ESLint configuration present at repo root).

4) Project-specific conventions and gotchas
- Import alias: always use `@/` for internal imports instead of relative paths to keep imports consistent.
- Route ordering: App routes are order-sensitive in the sense the comment in `src/App.tsx` explicitly asks to place custom routes above the catch-all `"*"` route.
- Local persistence: cart uses `localStorage` key `"cart"`. Modifying this key affects persisted dev state.
- Dev-only plugin: `lovable-tagger` is enabled in `vite.config.ts` when `mode === "development"`. Avoid changing plugin usage unless you understand Lovable tagging behavior.
- UI library: Components in `src/components/ui` may expect specific props patterns and variant usage via `class-variance-authority` (CVA). Reuse existing primitives where possible.

5) Integration points & external dependencies
- React Query: network and caching patterns assume usage of `@tanstack/react-query`. Look for `useQuery`/`useMutation` across pages.
- Routing: `react-router-dom` v6 — routes are element-based (no render/children props).
- Theme: `next-themes` is used for class-based theme toggling (root provider in `src/main.tsx`).

6) Helpful examples for edits and new code
- Add a new page:
  - Create `src/pages/MyPage.tsx`, implement default export component.
  - Add `<Route path="/my-page" element={<MyPage />} />` to `src/App.tsx` above the `"*"` route.
- Use a shared UI primitive:
  - `import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button";`
  - Follow existing variant usage from `src/components/ProductCard.tsx`.

7) Debugging tips
- Start dev server and watch console for Vite overlay errors: `npm run dev` (Windows PowerShell). Example commands:
```
npm i
npm run dev
```
- If a module resolution error occurs, confirm the `@` alias in `vite.config.ts` points to `./src`.

8) Where not to assume
- No tests or test runner configured — do not attempt to run `npm test` (not present).
- No server-side code or API contracts in this repo — integration with payments or backends is out-of-repo unless you find explicit environment files.

9) When modifying code, run:
```
npm run lint
npm run build
npm run preview
```
to validate code compiles and lints.
